# INFLUENZA VACCINATION RECOMMENDATIONS

Influenza Vaccine Outpatient and Inpatient Guidelines

Annual influenza vaccination is recommended for all persons aged 6 months and older without a specific contraindication.

Eggs and latex allergies are NOT considered contraindications to receiving the vaccine, the only contraindication to the flu vaccination is severe allergic reaction (i.e. Anaphylactic reactions).

---

References:

- Grohskopf et al., MMWR Recommendations and Reports, 2024, 73(5)1-25
- Minneapolis VAHCS Influenza Committee
Therapy:
## Inpatient

##### Recommend observing all patients for 15 minutes after receiving any influenza vaccine. A previous severe allergic reaction to influenza vaccine, regardless of the component suspected of being responsible for the reaction, is a contraindication to future receipt of ANY influenza vaccine.

### Outpatient (excluding ED) Vaccination Recommendations

#For age 65 or older, administer Fluad Adjuvanted Trivalent 0.5ml syringe.

#For age 64 or under, administer Afluria Trivalent 0.5ml syringe.

\*No patient specific order needed:

- Administer via standing order protocol or Clinical Reminder

Note: Use immunization template to document administration.

### Inpatient and ED Vaccination Recommendations

Influenza orders are part of the admission order set. For those who require an order due to admission order being discontinued/expired or if patient was admitted prior to influenza season, use the order below:
Influenza Vaccination Inpatient and ED 25/26

#For age 65 or older, administer Fluad Adjuvanted Trivalent 0.5ml syringe.

#For age 64 or under, administer Afluria Trivalent 0.5ml syringe.

Note: Use immunization template to document administration.

*Local guidance (Des Moines CDSS, Inpatient):*
Annual influenza vaccination is recommended for all persons aged 6 months and older without a specific contraindication.

Recommend observing all patients for 15 minutes after receipt of any influenza vaccine. A previous severe allergic reaction to influenza vaccine, regardless of the component suspected of being responsible for the reaction, is a contraindication to future receipt of ANY influenza vaccine.
Influenza Vaccination Recommendations:
Outpatient Vaccination:
For age 65 or older administer Fluzone HIGH DOSE Trivalent 0.5ml syringe.
For age 64 or under administer Flurix Trivalent 0.5ml syringe.
Inpatient and ED Vaccination:
Influenza is a protocolized immunization and does not require a medication order. It is driven by a clinical reminder. Nursing will utilize the "Immunization" Note in CPRS that links to all clinical reminders associated with immunizations. This note allows for correct charting of the vaccine, lot# and expiration date.
For age 65 or older administer Fluzone HIGH DOSE Trivalent 0.5ml syringe.
For age 64 or under administer Flurix Trivalent 0.5ml syringe.
